question.text:
How many binary colorings of the vertices of a regular hexagon are distinct up to rotation,
when reflections are not identified?
(A) 10 (B) 12 (C) 13 (D) 14 (E) 16

solution.text:

A rotation by k steps has gcd(6, k) cycles, hence fixes 2 colorings. The six counts are
64, 2, 4, 8, 4, 2. Their average is 84/6 = 14.

question.text:
What is the size of the conjugacy class of (1 2 3)(4 5) in S ?
5
(A) 10 (B) 15 (C) 20 (D) 30 (E) 60

solution.text:
A commuting permutation must preserve the two cycle supports since their sizes differ. It
acts by one of three rotations on the 3-cycle and one of two rotations on the 2-cycle, so the
centralizer has order 6. The class has size 5!/6 = 20.

question.text:
A group of order 27 acts on a set of 20 elements. What is the smallest possible number of ele-
ments fixed by every group element?
(A) 0 (B) 1 (C) 2 (D) 3 (E) 9

solution.text:
Orbit sizes divide 27, so every nontrivial orbit has size divisible by three. The number
of singleton orbits is therefore congruent to 20, or two, modulo three, and is at least two.
This is attainable: let the cyclic group of order 27 act through a quotient of order nine on
two disjoint nine-point orbits, fixing two further points.
